clue.text: A school with a learner resembling a snake

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
L is the learner-driver abbreviation, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: A school that has taken on a learner is compared, unflatteringly, to a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a group of sea creatures here, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Apodal is the zoological term for having no feet or limbs, as a snake has none.

clue.text: Paula, initially on the shelf, finally became fiancee?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so P comes before the shelf
initially tells us to take only the opening letter of Paula

parts.note: a ledge is a shelf

indicators.note: finally tells us to take only the closing letter of became

explanation.surface: Paula, once left on the shelf as an unmarried woman, has at last got engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the shelf' suggests spinsterhood, but it places P above a ledge. The question mark flags that a fiancee is only one kind of pledgee.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledgee is the person to whom a pledge is given, and a fiancee has received a promise of marriage.

clue.text: Bill baddie turned up in foreign city years ago

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the joined words bill and baddie are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a cad is a dishonourable man, a baddie

explanation.surface: A villain who ran up a bill turned up in some foreign city long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'years ago' points to the old spelling of the Bangladeshi capital, now written Dhaka.
explanation.definitionFit: Dacca was the former English spelling of Dhaka, capital of Bangladesh, so it is a city name of the past.

clue.text: Adult stuck in underground river embarrassed to be beaten

indicators.note: stuck in says the adult is lodged inside the river's name

parts.note: Lethe is the river of forgetfulness in the classical underworld
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult
being embarrassed makes you go red

explanation.surface: An adult trapped in a subterranean river is too embarrassed to admit defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: Lethe is the river of the classical underworld, not a cave stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathered is slang for thrashed, as if hit with a leather strap.

clue.text: OU officials using security devices to capture lines going to party

indicators.note: to capture says the bugs close round the lines and party

parts.note: bugs are listening devices used by security services

indicators.note: going to puts the party after the lines

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for lines
a do is a party

explanation.surface: University officials use surveillance gear to snare party-goers.
explanation.walkthrough: OU here is Oxford University, not the Open University.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulldogs are the proctors' attendants who enforce discipline at Oxford University.

clue.text: Little woman lands on an unknown place near Jerusalem

indicators.note: in a down clue, landing on something means sitting above it, so Beth comes first

parts.note: Beth is one of the March sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A small woman touches down on some unidentified spot near Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little woman' looks like a description of size; it means a character from Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethany is the biblical village on the Mount of Olives, home of Lazarus, a short distance from Jerusalem.

clue.text: Vegetables, glossy, beginning to droop

indicators.note: the beginning droops, falling from the top of this down entry to its foot

parts.note: sleek means glossy, smooth and shiny

explanation.surface: Shiny vegetables are starting to wilt.
explanation.walkthrough: The S that starts SLEEK drops to the bottom of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeks are onion-family vegetables with long white stems.

clue.text: Lack of activity from guy eating last of the fatty food

indicators.note: eating says the guy has the other letters within him

parts.note: a dude is a guy

indicators.note: last of tells us to take the final letter of the

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat used in cooking

explanation.surface: A man scoffing greasy food ends up idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' looks like part of a meal scene, but it is the signal that the guy surrounds the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Desuetude is the state of disuse, when something is no longer practised or active.

clue.text: Predator using open-mouthed stare to protect duck (not a sound!)

indicators.note: to protect says the stare wraps round the other letters

parts.note: to gawk is to stare open-mouthed
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A predator gawps protectively at a duck while staying silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is a cricket zero, giving O, not a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The goshawk is a large hawk that hunts birds and small mammals.

clue.text: Seductive types — snatchers seen on the loose

indicators.note: something on the loose is running free and out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alluring thieves have been spotted running free.
explanation.definitionFit: Enchantresses are women who charm and allure, seductive figures.

clue.text: Problem for patient with brain lesion — nurse keeps diagram with data

definitions.text: Problem for patient with brain lesion

indicators.note: keeps means the nurse holds the diagram inside her

parts.note: aia is an Indian or Asian nurse or nanny, a crossword favourite
a graph is a diagram plotting data

explanation.surface: A nurse looking after a brain-damaged patient keeps a data chart.
explanation.walkthrough: An aia (or ayah) is a nurse or nanny in India, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Agraphia is loss of the ability to write, caused by damage to the brain.

clue.text: Place, one out of the way, by lake with aged stones

indicators.note: by sets the lake beside what comes before
out of the way says the one is removed from the place

parts.note: a site is a place
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the map abbreviation for lake
AE is short for aetatis, aged, as on gravestones

explanation.surface: A remote spot beside a lake has some ancient stones.
explanation.walkthrough: AE abbreviates the Latin aetatis, 'aged', found on memorials.
explanation.definitionFit: Stelae are upright carved stone slabs, used as monuments in the ancient world.

clue.text: Something steamy bloke reported

indicators.note: reported means we hear the word rather than read it

parts.note: a geezer is British slang for a bloke, a man

explanation.surface: A man was said to be up to something racy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steamy' hints at a racy story, but it is literal steam; a geezer is London slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser is a hot spring that throws out jets of water and vapour.

clue.text: Outfit that could be out of this world

definitions.text: Outfit that could be out of this world

parts.words: Outfit that could be out of this world
parts.note: out of this world usually praises clothing as wonderful, but here it means worn literally beyond Earth

explanation.walkthrough: 'out of this world' reads as praise for a stunning outfit; taken literally it is clothing for travel beyond Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts wear a pressurised suit to survive outside the Earth's atmosphere.

clue.text: Murky ale is off — it may go to someone's head

definitions.text: it may go to someone's head

indicators.note: beer that is off has gone bad, so these letters are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Cloudy beer has gone off, and drink may go to your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go to someone's head' suggests drink after the ale, but it means something worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarmulke is the skullcap worn by Jewish men, placed on the crown of the head.

clue.text: Lying about copper and maiden getting corrupt

parts.note: re means about, concerning
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
bent is slang for corrupt

explanation.surface: A policeman and a young woman are telling lies and being corrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' looks like telling untruths, but it means lying down; 'copper' is the metal, not a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent describes someone reclining or lying down.

clue.text: Like a rope cut off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: made of twisted strands, as a rope is

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are unrelated: one about fibres, one about being marooned.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranded describes rope twisted from strands, and also someone marooned without means of leaving.

clue.text: Bird is a layer — 100 eggs laid for starters

parts.note: a tier is a layer or row
C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: for starters tells us to take the opening letters of eggs and laid

explanation.surface: A hen that lays is credited with a hundred eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' looks like a laying hen, but it is a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiercel is a male hawk, especially a male peregrine falcon.

clue.text: Fund-raiser with no merriment contrived formal introduction

indicators.note: contrived means put together artificially, so the remaining letters are rearranged
with no means the merriment is taken away

parts.note: taken as written, the letters of fund-raiser
fun is merriment

explanation.surface: A joyless charity appeal opens with a stiff letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing FUN leaves DRAISER, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear Sir is the conventional formal salutation that opens a letter.

clue.text: Bad feeling of indigenous Canadians keeping quiet

indicators.note: keeping means the Crees hold the quiet letter inside

parts.note: the Cree are a First Nations people of Canada
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: Native Canadians keeping silent stirs unease.
explanation.definitionFit: The creeps is an idiom for a feeling of nervous unease or revulsion.

clue.text: Favourite place for students with a particular garden plant

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
uni is short for university

explanation.surface: A favourite student haunt has its own special plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The petunia is a popular bedding flower grown in gardens and hanging baskets.

clue.text: Man of principle wanting little son to be safe, safe, …

definitions.note: the definition is plural: a list of several safes

indicators.note: wanting here means needing, so the man needs the son added after him

parts.note: Laurence J Peter formulated the Peter Principle, that people rise to their level of incompetence
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A principled man misses his small boy and wants him safe.
explanation.walkthrough: A peter is criminal slang for a safe, so the list 'safe, safe, …' is several of them; the Peter Principle is the theory that staff rise to their level of incompetence.
explanation.definitionFit: In thieves' slang a peter is a strongbox, so a string of strongboxes makes the plural.

clue.text: Smart coastal holiday region? Sort of!

parts.note: SW is the south-west of England, with its holiday coastline of Devon and Cornwall
-ish means sort of, more or less

explanation.surface: A fashionable seaside resort area, or something like it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of!' looks like a hedge on the whole clue, but it supplies the ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal British for fashionable and expensive-looking.

clue.text: Fossil of an arachnid one day found lying hidden

indicators.note: lying hidden means the day is concealed within the arachnid

parts.note: a mite is a tiny arachnid
Mon is short for Monday

explanation.surface: A spider-like creature from a single day has been found buried as a fossil.
explanation.definitionFit: An ammonite is the coiled shell of an extinct sea mollusc, a common fossil.

clue.text: Spirit of a Parisian revolutionary leading soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue, leading puts this before the soldiers
revolutionary means turned round, so the French word is written backwards

parts.note: un is French for a
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A French rebel heading a troop has the right spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' evokes the French Revolution, but it reverses UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Numen is a presiding divinity or spirit dwelling in a place or object.

clue.text: Sue's romancing upset members of the family

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sue's love affair has unsettled her relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Cousins-german are first cousins, children of siblings, so close relatives.

clue.text: Christian possibly felt awkward with praise losing core element

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy and out of order, so these letters are rearranged
losing means the core element drops out

parts.note: to cheer someone is to praise them
one of the central letters of cheer

explanation.surface: A Christian was uneasy about praise that lacked substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' suggests a believer, but it is the surname of Fletcher Christian, the Bounty mutineer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fletcher Christian led the mutiny on HMS Bounty, so his forename pairs with that surname.

clue.text: Worry not about language

indicators.note: about means turned round, so worry and not are read backwards together

parts.note: to nag is to worry or pester

explanation.surface: Don't fret over the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongan is the Polynesian tongue spoken in the Pacific kingdom of Tonga.
